newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler buys 25 pct of Ballard.
newsitem.headline: Daimler buys 25 pct of Ballard.

text.p: German industrial group Daimler-Benz AG said on Monday it has bought a 25 percent stake in Canada-based Ballard Power Systems and they will jointly develop fuels cells for future electric vehicles.
Daimler said the companies would invest about 400 million marks into the fuel cell technology for research and development as well as to bring a product to the market.
Daimler, maker of Mercedes luxury vehicles, said the deal between the two companies calls for it to take the 25 percent stake in Ballard through a capital-raising measure.

In addition, the two companies will form a new venture to bring the alternative energy engines to market in which Daimler will hold a two-thirds stake and Ballard a one-third stake, Daimler said in a statement.

Ballard, based in Vancouver, and Daimler began joint efforts in 1993 to further develop Ballard's proprietary zero-emission engine that converts natural gas, methanol or hydrogen fuel into electricity without combustion.

Daimler management board member Juergen Hubber, who oversees Mercedes' passenger vehicle division, said the Ballard motor had "the greatest chance at the moment" to compete against the conventional gasoline-powered motor.
Daimler said the deal would require approval from cartel authorities as well as by shareholders in Ballard at an annual general meeting on May 29.
